content: Fluticasone nasal spray is prescribed to alleviate symptoms associated with seasonal allergic rhinitis, perennial allergic rhinitis, and perennial nonallergic rhinitis. These symptoms may include sneezing, nasal congestion, runny nose, and nasal itching. Fluticasone belongs to a class of medications known as corticosteroids, which function by reducing and preventing inflammation in the nasal passages. Fluticasone nasal spray is available as a liquid formulation intended for intranasal use. It is typically administered once or twice daily, either in the morning or both morning and evening. In some cases, it may be used on an as-needed basis to manage symptoms. It is essential to follow the instructions provided on the prescription label precisely. Do not use more or less of the medication or use it more frequently than prescribed. This medication is strictly for nasal use and should not be swallowed or sprayed into the eyes. Physicians often initiate treatment with a higher dose and may reduce the dosage once symptoms are under control. While fluticasone can effectively manage rhinitis symptoms, it does not cure the underlying condition. Symptom relief may not be noticeable for at least 12 hours after the first use, and it may take several days or longer to experience the full therapeutic benefits. Regular use is recommended for optimal results, and treatment should not be discontinued without consulting a healthcare provider. Each bottle of fluticasone nasal spray is designed to deliver 120 sprays. After 120 sprays, the bottle should be discarded, even if it still contains liquid, as the dosage per spray may no longer be accurate. To use the nasal spray, follow these steps: 1. Shake the bottle gently. 2. Remove the dust cover. 3. If using the pump for the first time or after a week or more of inactivity, prime it by pressing and releasing the pump six times (or until a fine mist appears). If the pump has been used within the past week, skip this step. 4. Blow your nose to clear your nostrils. 5. Close one nostril with your finger. 6. Tilt your head slightly forward and insert the nasal applicator into the other nostril, keeping the bottle upright. 7. Begin to inhale through your nose. 8. While inhaling, press firmly on the applicator to release a spray. 9. Breathe gently through the nostril and exhale through your mouth. 10. If a second spray is required in the same nostril, repeat the process. 11. Repeat the procedure for the other nostril. 12. After use, clean the applicator with a tissue and replace the dust cover. Fluticasone may also be prescribed for other medical conditions. Consult your healthcare provider or pharmacist for additional information. Before using fluticasone nasal spray, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to fluticasone or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or have recently taken. Certain medications, such as antifungals, HIV protease inhibitors, and oral steroids, may interact with fluticasone, necessitating dose adjustments or close monitoring for side effects. Additionally, disclose any history of tuberculosis, cataracts, glaucoma, nasal sores, untreated infections, or herpes infections in the eye. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone nasal surgery or sustained a nasal injury. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform the healthcare provider that you are using fluticasone. If transitioning from oral steroids to fluticasone, your doctor may gradually reduce your oral steroid dose. During this adjustment period, monitor for symptoms such as extreme fatigue, muscle weakness, abdominal pain, appetite loss, weight loss, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, depression, or skin darkening, and report them to your doctor immediately. Your body may have a reduced ability to handle stress during this time, so inform all healthcare providers of your recent medication change and consider wearing a medical identification bracelet. Fluticasone may weaken the immune system, increasing susceptibility to infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious illnesses, such as chickenpox or measles, and notify your doctor immediately if you are exposed to these viruses. Discuss with your doctor whether it is safe to consume grapefruit juice while using this medication. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to compensate for a missed one. Minor side effects of fluticasone may include headaches, nosebleeds, nasal irritation, runny nose, bloody nasal mucus, coughing, upset stomach, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and dizziness. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, require immediate medical attention. These include painful white patches in the nose or throat, flu-like symptoms, sore throat, vision changes, nasal injuries, new or worsening acne, easy bruising, facial or neck swelling, extreme fatigue, muscle weakness, irregular menstrual cycles, hives, rash, itching, swelling of the face or extremities, hoarseness, difficulty breathing or swallowing, and wheezing. Fluticasone may also slow growth in children, though its impact on final adult height is unclear. Discuss the risks with your child’s doctor. Report any unusual symptoms to your healthcare provider. Store fluticasone in its original container, tightly sealed, at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, consulting your pharmacist if needed. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the individual has collapsed or is not breathing. Symptoms of long-term overuse may include facial or neck swelling, acne, easy bruising, extreme fatigue, muscle weakness, irregular menstrual cycles, appetite loss, weight loss, irritability, depression, dizziness, fainting, or skin darkening. Keep all medical appointments and clean the nasal spray applicator weekly. Remove the dust cap and applicator, wash them in warm water, let them air dry, and reassemble. If the applicator becomes clogged, soak it in warm water, rinse with cold water, and dry it. Do not use sharp objects to clear blockages. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist with any questions about refills. Fluticasone is marketed under the brand name Flonase® Nasal Spray.
